_comment: Deterministic clean-up applied to a generated report before it is returned.
Templates carry fill-in markers (XX, ****, '(grade )') and conditional lines
whose reason has to be dictated ('This study is suboptimal due to ...').
_STRUCTURE_SYS instructs the model to fill or drop these, and it usually
does -- but 'usually' is the wrong reliability for a line that asserts a
study was suboptimal without saying why, or reports a measurement as a
literal 'XX'. Both read as findings to a clinician skimming the report.
Each pattern is a Python regular expression matched case-insensitively
against a single stripped line. A matching line is REMOVED. Patterns must
therefore describe residue only -- text that cannot occur once the line has
been properly filled in. Adding a pattern here is a clinical-safety change:
an over-broad one silently deletes real findings.
Set REPORT_POSTPROCESS=0 to disable this pass entirely.

drop_line_patterns.why: Unfilled measurement placeholders: 'XX' / 'XXX' as a standalone token, e.g. '(Lt=XX, Rt=XX mm)'. Real reports carry digits here.
Redaction runs the template uses where a referral target belongs, e.g. 'correlation with ******* is recommended'.
A severity/grade parenthesis left empty, e.g. 'fatty liver (grade )'.

A conditional limitation line whose reason was never dictated, so it runs straight from 'due to' into the clause that should have followed the reason -- 'This study is suboptimal due to; however:' or '... due to however:'.
Any surviving alternative marker. The model is told to pick exactly one line per group and drop the leading '*'; a line still starting with one is a template dump, not a finding.
